newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says Labour tax plan to cost 8 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says Labour tax plan to cost 8 bln stg.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke dismissed the Labour party's pledge to introduce a 10 percent basic income tax rate in the long term as "incredible and irresponsible."
"This would cost more than eight billion pounds -- money that would have to be found elsewhere from higher taxes or public spending cuts," he said in a statement.
"Labour cannot and will not say No to raising the basic rate, raising the higher rate or introducing a new top rate."
"As night follows day, the tax burden would rise if Britain ever elected a Labour government," Clarke added.

In a statement released ahead of a news conference, the Chancellor said Labour aimed to take away the 700 pounds of extra disposable income he said the average family enjoyed as a result of recent government measures.
He said the ruling Conservatives would attack Labour's planned windfall tax on the profits of privatised utilities.
"We will expose the myth that a utilities tax is a painless tax. It will be equivalent to two pence on the standard rate of income tax." -- Mariam Isa, London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774
